I am a quantitative researcher interested in **climate risk, environmental data science, systems modelling, and quantitative approaches to climate adaptation and mitigation planning**.

I completed the Integrated BS–MS programme at IISER Pune, with research spanning high-resolution climate reanalysis, nonlinear heat-stress metrics, statistical trend analysis, network methods, and agent-based modelling.

A recurring theme in my work is that quantitative frameworks are not neutral containers for facts. **Metric definitions, thresholds, aggregation scales, model objectives, and the populations represented can encode normative and political choices.** I try to make those choices visible rather than hide them behind technical defaults. I think of this as a form of **normatively grounded quantitative modelling**.

My current climate research develops that perspective through heat-stress measurement and aggregation. I am increasingly interested in carrying it into systems models that connect physical hazards and exposure with infrastructure, interventions, resources, behaviour, adaptation, mitigation, and policy choices.
